I checked each of the correction protocol's eight builder rules against build_sand_survey_pass4_correction.py (commit 8fa0e860), reading it next to the pass-4 builder, both earlier protocols, the reader prompt read_pass4.js, the input preparation and its outputs, and the red team summary. The repo test file passes: 20 passed (pytest -p no:cacheprovider, basetemp in scratch).

The builder runs without crashing on the real committed inputs. I ran it from scratch/review_correction_builder/real with copies of the P2/P3 records, the survey4 and survey4c text dirs, and no correction readings yet. It reported: pass-4 list 28 READ, 5 SKIMMED (B04 B05 B07 B11 B12), 1 UNFETCHABLE (B23); 52 of 52 element quotes found; E4 at distance one B14 and B22, E5 B01; leads 94 raw, 22 dropped, 72 kept; conjunction RETIRED, which matches how the pass-2 and pass-3 records applied it.

Synthetic edge cases are in scratch/review_correction_builder/harness.py and extra.py. The harness uses the test file's build() helper plus a titles override. Run them with PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python harness.py [A|B|C|D|E|F|I|L|M|O] and python extra.py.

These cases hold:
- A SKIMMED source's all-five RETIRES is recorded as OCCUPIES from abstract, the reader's verdict is kept, and C4a stays OCCUPIED.
- A C2 RETIRES on a READ source with one confirmer, or with two identical confirmers, is DISPUTED: C2 UNPRICED, sentence UNLICENSED. With two distinct confirmers it retires: C2 RETIRED, sentence SURVIVES_WITHOUT_C2.
- A DISPUTED on C2 alone makes the sentence UNLICENSED.
- A located copy that failed leaves the landing page SKIMMED. A scope-listed source re-read with no located copy stays SKIMMED.
- Ties across elements name every tied source, and distance-one sources are named by element with no tie-break.
- With no source at distance one, every source at the smallest distance is named.
- Five names pass; six set UNLICENSED.
- The C4a pool takes no pass-3 element flags: p3 is read only for clause statuses and titles, and P3MAP is not imported.

Where the code departs from the protocol, the findings follow.

findings.title: A C4a RETIRES that does not carry E1-E5 is downgraded to OCCUPIES and its confirmations are never read; the protocol sends it to two confirmers and makes it DISPUTED or retired
findings.claim: Correction rule 3 (protocol lines 107-110) says 'a first reading carrying E1-E5 for C4a, or a RETIRES on any clause, needs two confirmers', and otherwise the source is DISPUTED. The pass-4 protocol says the same ('A RETIRES verdict stands only when two further readers ... each code E1 to E5 true. If either does not, the source is recorded DISPUTED'). The builder instead applies a rule that neither protocol states (docstring line 28-29, code lines 240-246): a C4a RETIRES whose elements are not all carried is rewritten to OCCUPIES. Because `candidate` is then False, the `elif candidate:` branch at line 252 never runs, so the confirmations the workflow collects for that RETIRES (read_pass4.js sends every RETIRES to two confirmers) are ignored. The source then enters the nearness pool at distance one and can be named in a licensed sentence. The repo test test_all_five_coded_with_one_unfound_quote_is_not_a_retirement_candidate (tests line 92-96) locks this behaviour in.
findings.evidence: harness.py case B. The first reading codes C4a RETIRES with E1-E5 true, and the E5 quote is not in the text. Confirmers confirmer-1 and confirmer-2 give distinct returns, and both carry E1-E5 with quotes found. Output: {"verdict": "OCCUPIES", "reader_verdict": "RETIRES", "verdict_note": "a C4a RETIRES that does not carry E1-E5 is recorded as OCCUPIES", "distance": 1, "confirmations": null}, C4a OCCUPIED, sentence SURVIVES, named ["PA"], text '... (where PA authors audit served models, without log-probabilities) ...'. Under rule 3 this is a confirmed retirement: C4a RETIRED, sentence RETIRED. Case B2 (same reading, no confirmations) gives verdict OCCUPIES, C4a OCCUPIED, sentence SURVIVES, disputed []. Rule 3 requires DISPUTED, which means sentence UNLICENSED. The realistic trigger: a reader who codes all five true and writes RETIRES, as the prompt instructs, with one quote failing normalisation.
findings.suggested_repair: Treat any first-reader RETIRES on C4a as a retirement candidate, as for C2 and C5: take the confirmations, require each confirmer to carry E1-E5 by rule 2 and pass both proofs, record RETIRES if two distinct confirmers do and DISPUTED otherwise. Keep the first reader's element coding and distance for the record. Replace the test that asserts OCCUPIED with one asserting DISPUTED (no confirmers) and RETIRED (two carrying confirmers).

findings.title: A confirmation identical to the first reader's own return counts as a distinct confirmer
findings.claim: Rule 3 (new) requires confirmers 'distinct from each other and from the first reader'. The builder tells confirmers apart from each other by name and by content hash (lines 264-269). Its check against the first reader, though, is only `x["confirmer"] != r["reader"]` (line 264), which compares strings like 'run:confirmer-k' with 'run:reader-i'; under read_pass4.js's naming those can never be equal. The first reading is never content-hashed, so a copy of the first reader's verdict filed as a confirmation counts as an independent confirmer. By the builder's own standard (line 267: one return under two names is one confirmation), such a copy is the first reader.
findings.evidence: harness.py case C4. PA's first reading is C2 RETIRES (object 'o', reason 'r', with its last line and midpoint). One confirmation carries exactly those fields under the name confirmer-1, and one distinct confirmation is from confirmer-2 (reason 'r2'). Output: {"v": "RETIRES", "carrying": ["pass4/readings:confirmer-1", "pass4/readings:confirmer-2"], "C2": "RETIRED"}. The expected result is DISPUTED, since only one confirmer is distinct from the first reader. extra.py case N2 shows the name check fires only when the confirmer is literally named 'reader-1'.
findings.suggested_repair: Also hash the first reader's verdict for that clause (with the same fields: verdict, elements, object, reason, last-line and midpoint quotes), exclude any confirmation whose hash matches it, and test that case.

The behaviour reproduces, but whether it breaks the protocol depends on how you read it, and it has no effect on any status or sentence.

**Reproduction.** Script: scratchpad\review_correction_builder\sk_skim_silent_all5.py, which uses the test file's build() and reading() helpers.
- **Case A.** PA is SKIMMED by scope, C4a is SILENT, and E1-E5 are coded true with their quotes found. Output: verdict OCCUPIES, reader_verdict SILENT, distance 0, skimmed_rule set, from_abstract True. The C4a bucket has occupied_from_abstract_by ['PA'] and silent [].
- **Case B (control).** SILENT with only four elements coded. The SILENT is kept (silent ['PA']).
- In both cases C4a is OCCUPIED and the sentence is SURVIVES.
- The cause is builder lines 241 and 247-250. For C4a, candidate = (distance == 0) whatever the verdict word, and on a non-READ source any candidate is rewritten to OCCUPIES.

**Why this may not be a defect.**
1. The pass-4 protocol still holds under the correction (correction protocol lines 7-8). Its line 60 defines the verdict by elements: "A source RETIRES C4a when it carries E1 to E5". So a C4a reading that carries E1-E5 is, by the frozen definition, a retirement claim. Correction rule 3 (line 107) agrees: "a first reading carrying E1-E5 for C4a, or a RETIRES on any clause, needs two confirmers". The builder treats a READ SILENT with all five the same way and sends it to confirmers.
2. On that reading, rule 1's "A RETIRES from a SKIMMED source is recorded as OCCUPIES from abstract, with the reader's original verdict kept beside it" covers this case. The builder does exactly that: it keeps reader_verdict SILENT beside the new verdict.
3. The inherited 2026-09-13 rule (line 48) allows a SKIMMED source to be SILENT or OCCUPIES from abstract, so the recorded outcome is permitted. SILENT is defined as "does not address the clause" (line 46), and a reading with five verified element quotes plainly addresses it.
4. The builder's docstring (lines 23-24) states the rule openly.

**Where it does depart.** Rule 1 says literally that a SILENT is kept, so the finding is not refuted outright.

**Severity is at most minor.**
- An OCCUPIES from abstract never retires or unprices a clause.
- The nearness pool (line 313) and the conjunction's does-all set (line 330) take READ sources only.
- So only the bucket label and verdict field change, never a status, count or sentence.
- The real returns cannot trigger it. Script sk_real_skim_silent.py scanned readings_run_A, B1, B2, B3 and readings_correction_run1: none has a C4a reading coded E1-E5 all true or any C4a RETIRES. The scoped sources are B04, B05, B07, B11 and B12.

findings.title: Europe PMC lookups fail silently; the committed B23 record misstates what Europe PMC holds
findings.claim: curl_json swallows every parse or network failure and returns {"_unparsed": ...}. The callers then turn that into None. So a failed query reads in the record exactly like a query that found nothing. For B23 the committed located_by reports Europe PMC with pmid None, but Europe PMC does hold the article, so the lookup failed at run time and was recorded as tried and empty. B04's "PMCID found: None" cannot be checked for the same reason. The protocol's 'PubMed Central by its PMID' route is also carried out only as a Europe PMC search, with the PMID hard-coded and its source not recorded.

Refuse, or record an explicit error, when the response does not parse, instead of defaulting to None. Correct B23's located_by to pmid 41955357, inEPMC N, hasPDF N. verdicts.reason:

Lines 106 and 108 then turn that into pmcid None and an empty hit, and the f-string at lines 125-126 prints the Europe PMC part of located_by as "Europe PMC None pmcid None full text None/None". So a failed call and a real zero-hit search leave the same record.

I re-ran the three queries today with curl:
- The DOI:"10.1126/science.aeh8588" core search returns hitCount 1: pmid 41955357, pmcid None, inEPMC N, inPMC N, hasPDF N, firstIndexDate 2026-04-10. That is well before the run, whose attempts are stamped 2026-09-15T02:07Z.

So the committed B23 string misstates what Europe PMC held. The run cannot tell a failure from a real zero-hit result, because no raw response was saved. B04's "PMCID found: None" agrees with today's result but cannot be checked against the run itself.

PMID 42323341 appears nowhere in the worktree's papers/plates tree except in the prepare script and the record it wrote, so its source is not recorded. The protocol names "PubMed Central by its PMID" (line 59). The script checks that only by searching Europe PMC and would fetch the fullTextXML only if a PMCID came back. That is a reasonable way to do it, since Europe PMC mirrors PMC, but the record does not say so.

I looked for a reading under which this is not a defect. The status is unaffected: B23 has no PMCID and no full text (inEPMC N, hasPDF N), so it stays UNFETCHABLE; B04 has no PMCID, so no PMC route exists. The protocol does not require raw responses to be recorded. What fails is the record itself: it gives a wrong fact about a route the protocol fixed (B23's Europe PMC row), and it cannot be audited. No status, count or reader-facing sentence changes, so minor is the right severity, not overstated.

findings.title: The same-page guard is a rule the protocol does not state, and it only catches byte-identical text
findings.claim: The protocol accepts a located copy 'that carries the listed title' and sends it through fetch_pass4.py. The script adds same_text_as_the_pass4_page, which refuses a route only when its extracted text hashes the same as pass 4's landing-page text. That rule decided B04. Any landing page whose visible text differs by one character (a date, a session id, a banner) passes the title and length checks and is accepted as FETCHED with located_for_scope. The builder then treats it as a located copy that was read (located_read, builder line 224) and lifts the scope file's SKIMMED, so a landing page would be recorded READ again, which is the red team's finding 3. B04's outcome was correct only because Nature served the same text twice.
findings.suggested_repair: Disclose the same-page rule in the CORRECTION as a rule applied beyond the frozen text. Also record, for every accepted located copy, evidence that it is the article's text rather than a page: content_type, page count, and article-body markers such as an Abstract or a References section. At minimum, refuse an HTML located response whose url_effective is the pass-4 landing URL instead of comparing text hashes.

verdicts.reason:
I reproduced the weakness, but it had no effect on the committed inputs, and half of the claim is overstated. **Reproduced.** I ran scratchpad/review_correction_builder/p_samepage.py, which repeats the acceptance test in prepare_correction_inputs.py lines 145-151. - On the real B04.located.0.bin it gives chars 9648, title_words_found 1.0 and same_text_as_the_pass4_page True, so accepted is False. - With `

1

` inserted before `` it gives chars 9652, title_words_found 1.0 and same_text False, so accepted is True. The guard compares one sha256 of the extracted text with pass 4's fulltext.sha256 (ac09ddc8..., 9648 chars, fetch_record_run_B2.json). It checks nothing else: not content_type, not pages, not url_effective. The pass-4 page and the located attempt arrived with different cookie codes in url_effective (code=924b9130... against code=1a8bd6ff...). Only the visible text happened to match. **The builder chain holds.** - B04 is in the pass-4 fetched_text_scope.json, and so are B05 and B07. - merge_fetch (builder lines 126-136) takes a correction record marked FETCHED and located_for_scope over the pass-4 page. - Lines 224-228 set located_read, which skips the SKIMMED downgrade. - The test at tests/test_build_sand_survey_pass4_correction.py:210-218 asserts READ for such a source. So a landing page with slightly different text that the reader proves read would be recorded READ. That is red-team finding 3. **Why minor, not more.** 1. The script already ran, and its outputs were committed at 382935c4 before any reading. On those inputs the guard gave the correct result: - B04 was refused and is UNFETCHABLE, so the pass-4 page stays in force. - B05, B07 and B11 were accepted as application/pdf with 15, 15 and 4 pages, from the exact URLs in the protocol's table. - No committed status, count or sentence is wrong. The weakness matters only if the preparation is run again. 2. "A rule the protocol does not state" is overstated. The frozen correction protocol, under "Scope: text that is not the article", says a landing page is not the article. Refusing a route that leads back to the pass-4 landing page applies that definition. It is not a new rule: it narrows what counts as "a located copy that carries the listed title". Each attempt also records it in fetch_record_correction.json as same_text_as_the_pass4_page. The real defect is that the guard is fragile, not that it goes beyond the protocol.

findings.title: NOT_RECODED reaches the builder as UNFETCHABLE, making C4a UNPRICED and the sentence UNLICENSED
findings.claim: The protocol says an earlier source whose bytes do not match 'is not read, and is recorded as not re-coded'. The script writes status NOT_RECODED, a word the builder does not know. The builder treats every status other than FETCHED as UNFETCHABLE and codes C4a UNCHECKABLE, which prices C4a UNPRICED and makes the whole sentence UNLICENSED. That outcome is stronger than the protocol's 'not re-coded'. The script also adds a second NOT_RECODED ground the protocol does not name: a title or length check on pass-2 texts, written without a reason field. No committed source hits either path; all 23 are FETCHED.
findings.evidence:
prepare_correction_inputs.py lines 81, 86 ("FETCHED" if (len(text) > 1500 and frac >= 0.6) else "NOT_RECODED", no reason) and 97.

Builder lines 201-204 (status != FETCHED -> UNFETCHABLE, verdict UNCHECKABLE), 294-305 (uncheckable -> UNPRICED) and 345-346 (C4a UNPRICED -> sentence UNLICENSED).

review_correction_builder/p_notrecoded.py runs the test file's build() helper:
- control: "SA status: READ ... C4a status: OCCUPIED ... sentence: SURVIVES"
- with c_fetch SA status NOT_RECODED: "SA status: UNFETCHABLE ... C4a status: UNPRICED | correction buckets: {'occupied_by': ['PA'], 'uncheckable': ['SA']} ... sentence: UNLICENSED".
findings.suggested_repair: Have the builder recognise NOT_RECODED. Record such a source under a not_recoded list, keep its earlier-pass verdict out of the pool, and do not unprice the clause. Or have the builder refuse on an unknown fetch status. Drop the title and length ground at prepare line 86, or record a reason when it fires.

verdicts.reason:
I reproduced this, with one correction to the evidence. Line 81 of prepare_correction_inputs.py does write a reason ("... does not match its record"). Line 97 writes one too. Only the title-and-length ground at line 86 writes NOT_RECODED with no reason.

What the builder does: build_sand_survey_pass4_correction.py lines 201-204 test status != "FETCHED". Any such source becomes UNFETCHABLE with verdict UNCHECKABLE. Lines 294-305 put it in the uncheckable bucket, so C4a becomes UNPRICED. Lines 345-346 then make the sentence UNLICENSED. Grep shows no NOT_RECODED or not_recoded anywhere in the builder, the pass-4 builder or the tests.

Run: scratchpad/review_correction_builder/p_notrecoded.py, which uses the test file's build() helper with REPO set to the worktree.
- Control: SA READ, C4a OCCUPIED (occupied_by PA, SA), sentence SURVIVES.
- SA given status NOT_RECODED: SA UNFETCHABLE, C4a verdicts {'C4a': {'verdict': 'UNCHECKABLE'}}, C4a UNPRICED (uncheckable ['SA']), sentence UNLICENSED ("the fingerprint clause is UNPRICED"). counts.recoded_status also reports UNFETCHABLE: 1.

This departs from the frozen protocol. Correction protocol line 80 says such a source "is recorded as not re-coded". The same protocol uses UNFETCHABLE as its own separate status, for example for B23 at line 64. The builder instead records the source as UNFETCHABLE.

The line-86 gate (text over 1500 characters and title-word fraction of at least 0.6) is a NOT_RECODED ground the protocol does not name. The protocol's only ground is bytes that do not match the record. Because line 86 writes no reason, builder line 203 would fill unfetchable_reason with "no fetch record", which is false: a fetch record exists.

Why only minor:
- The protocol never says how a not-re-coded source affects pricing. The inherited rule (PROTOCOL_sand_prior_art_2026_09_13.md lines 49-53) prices an unchecked candidate as UNPRICED, so UNPRICED/UNLICENSED can be read as the cautious outcome rather than a forbidden one. The clear departures are the status label, the false reason text and the extra ground.
- No real input reaches this path. The committed fetch_record_correction.json has all 23 earlier-pass sources FETCHED (S11-S19 and L01-L15; S19 has title fraction 0.75, L15 has 10133 characters). The three UNFETCHABLE entries are the located routes for B04, B12 and B23.
